alpha_estimate.evidence: The document presents a framework where justice (accountability, cost acknowledgment) and mercy (grace from outside, restoration) are both fully present and balanced. The Salvation Algorithm (GS-03) and Why Grace Has to Come from Outside (GS-04) explicitly show that justice requires cost payment and mercy provides it, with the judge (God) bearing the cost, achieving a balanced alpha near 0.5.

accountability.evidence: The framework holds all beings accountable to the moral law derived from physics (e.g., GS-15 Holding God Accountable, GS-19 Salvation Narrative: 10 Laws). No one escapes the standard.

cost_acknowledgment.evidence: The entire framework is built on acknowledging the real cost of sin/entropy (GS-04, GS-17). The Second Law is treated as a non-negotiable reality.

consequence_honesty.evidence: Heaven and Hell are described as attractor states (GS-05) — honest about eternal consequences without softening.

standard_clarity.evidence: The 24 properties of God (GS-01) and 24 anti-properties (GS-16) provide a clear, measurable standard.

proportionality.evidence: The punishment (separation) is proportional to the rejection of the source of life; the cross provides exactly the needed cost.

compassion.evidence: The entire narrative is driven by God's love and desire to restore (GS-03, GS-04). The cross is the ultimate act of compassion.

restoration_focus.evidence: Salvation is described as a phase transition (GS-18) — not just punishment avoidance but actual restoration to original design.

grace_extension.evidence: Grace is unearned and comes from outside the system (GS-04). The Salvation Algorithm is offered freely.

record_preservation.evidence: The cross preserves the record of sin (justice is satisfied) while offering mercy. The truth is not erased but paid for.

cost_bearing.evidence: God the Son bears the full cost of sin on the cross (GS-19, GS-22). The judge pays the penalty.

vengeance.evidence: No surplus punishment. The cost is exactly paid, not exceeded.

enabling.evidence: Consequences are fully acknowledged; no pretending sin doesn't matter.

self_righteousness.evidence: God is held accountable (GS-15) and the framework admits human inability to self-save.

cheap_grace.evidence: Grace costs God everything (the cross). It is not cheap.

scapegoating.evidence: The cost is borne willingly by the judge, not transferred to an unwilling party.

poor_in_spirit.evidence: Acknowledges human inability to save oneself (GS-04).

mourning.evidence: Grieves the brokenness of the world and the cost of sin (GS-02, GS-05).

meekness.evidence: God's power is under control, exercised in self-sacrifice (the cross).

hunger_for_righteousness.evidence: Actively pursues justice through the moral law and accountability (GS-15, GS-19).

merciful.evidence: Extends mercy at personal cost (the cross).

pure_in_heart.evidence: Single-minded integrity: God's character is consistent across all domains (GS-01, GS-12).

peacemaker.evidence: Reconciles justice and mercy, God and humanity (GS-03, GS-19).

persecuted.evidence: Maintains position despite cost (the cross, and the document's claim that consensus is often wrong (GS-14)).

diagnosis: This document presents a fully integrated justice-mercy framework where both are maximized simultaneously through the cross configuration. It avoids all anti-patterns and meets all beatitude thresholds, achieving near-perfect alignment with the R(offense, alpha) spectrum.
strongest_moment: The explicit statement that the judge (God) pays the cost of the offense (the cross), satisfying both justice and mercy maximally.
biggest_gap: While the framework is comprehensive, some readers may find the connection between physical laws and moral properties abstract; more concrete examples of how this plays out in daily life could strengthen the mercy metrics further.
